about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Old-crop Mar is pushing back above 81-82 as Dec heads into delivery, with Texas Plains drought losses still the supply story; nothing new on export demand. A slightly softer dollar and a firmer real today ease the Brazil export-competition headwind at the margin; watch high-grade certificated stocks into Dec notice, which are not benign for longs.
events: Cotton firm, Dec ~78.7 and Mar ~82 midday (Yahoo Finance/ICE)
Texas Plains drought cuts dryland yields (Farm Progress)
Mar/May spread in focus as Dec delivery nears (Barchart)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil remains the driver: the real bounced about 1% to near 5.89 after Lula's fiscal plan cleared Congress, trimming some of the mill-hedging incentive that weighed last week. Mar is holding just above 17.56 resistance, but nothing has changed in Brazil's supply picture, so the bounce still reads as positioning.
events: Lula's fiscal plan clears Congress after real slump (Bloomberg)
Raw sugar holds Monday's rebound near 17.6 (Barchart)

coffee.fundamental: Rising ICE certified arabica stocks remain the bearish anchor and ease Dec deliverability worries; a firmer real today only slightly reduces Brazilian farmer selling. USDA's cut to Colombia's export outlook trims washed-arabica availability, a modest offset rather than a change of direction.
events: USDA cuts Colombia coffee export forecast by 760,000 bags (Daily Coffee News)
Real rebounds as fiscal plan passes (Bloomberg)

cocoa.fundamental: Recent reports point to Ivory Coast port arrivals picking up after rain-related transport delays, and talk of ample global supply is weighing on prices; rising ICE certified stocks support that. Offsets are El Niño risk to the mid-crop and EUDR-related premiums in Europe; no new Ghana COCOBOD news since the 2030 bean-export-ban plan.
events: Cocoa eases as supply concerns fade and arrivals improve (Barchart/Nasdaq)
EUDR preparations lift European cocoa premiums (Bloomberg)
El Niño risk flagged for West African output (ADMIS)
